title: Long Intervals Without Distinct Multiples of the First $n$ Positive Integers
summary: For positive integers $n$ and $m$, let $f(n,m)$ be the least integer $h\ge0$ such that $(m,m+h]$ contains distinct integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfying $i\mid a_i$ for $1\le i\le n$, and put $F(n)=\max_{m\in\mathbb{N}} f(n,m)$. A recent theorem of van Doorn [INTEGERS, 2026; arXiv:2601.16972] gives $F(n)-f(n,n)>0.36\,n\log n/\log\log n$ for sufficiently large $n$.
